title: Database migrations: schema changes verified on a disposable PostgreSQL and applied on deploy with a backup
description:
Filed by architect-16a01670 from parent task-e7a3d643bde34da7b27495dbda745739 (epic breakdown, human-directed 2026-09-04; owner chose Stage 1 + Stage 2 scope).

VISION Stage 2 'database migrations' and the profile 'database schema and migrations'. Re-measured 2026-09-04: the verifier runs the node's `test` recipe in the workspace (apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/node-verifier.ts + verifier-process-runner.ts) with no database; no migration tooling in the scaffold profile; no migration receipt.

FEATURE: (a) the scaffold profile adopts one migration tool (architect picks drizzle-kit or node-pg-migrate; pinned) with `pnpm db:migrate` / `pnpm db:migrate:down` scripts and a `migrations/` directory; node missions that change schema must add a migration (the compiler emits the requirement; the mission text says so). (b) The verifier gains a DATABASE leg: when the workspace declares `db:migrate`, start a disposable PostgreSQL container (docker; random port), export DATABASE_URL to the recipe, run the migrations, then the tests, then tear the container down on every exit path. (c) Deploy applies pending migrations against the environment's database after a `pg_dump` backup (`<project>/.moe-next/backups/<env>/<ts>.sql`, sha256 in the receipt) and records `moe-migration-receipt/1` {environment, sha, applied[], backupRef, APPLIED|REFUSED(code)}; `deployment.migrate_down` (human-only) reverts the last batch or restores the backup. (d) UI: the Deployments card shows migration state per environment (pending/applied, last backup); Runs shows migration receipts; a node card shows 'adds migration 0007'. Refusals: MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING, MIGRATION_DB_UNAVAILABLE, MIGRATION_FAILED (with the failing file), MIGRATION_BACKUP_FAILED. Docker absent -> the DATABASE leg refuses MIGRATION_DB_UNAVAILABLE; the verifier never silently skips.
definitionOfDone: Verifier DATABASE leg: with a workspace declaring `db:migrate`, the test proves DATABASE_URL reached the recipe, migrations ran before the tests, and the container is gone after ACCEPT, after REJECT and after a forced kill; docker absent -> MIGRATION_DB_UNAVAILABLE asserted with code + layer (a skip with reason, never a silent pass).

Deploy migration: offline test through the docker/pg ports asserts backup-before-migrate ordering and the receipt (applied set, backupRef sha256); `deployment.migrate_down` reverts and its receipt records the restore.

Scaffold profile golden updated (migration tool, scripts, `migrations/` with an initial migration); the generated app's `pnpm db:migrate` runs green against the disposable PostgreSQL in a test (count line quoted).

`deployment.migrate_down` (and any migrate kind) published human-only, MCP-excluded, with the full roster backfill and bidirectional roster tests; MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING, MIGRATION_DB_UNAVAILABLE, MIGRATION_FAILED, MIGRATION_BACKUP_FAILED asserted with code + layer.

Deployments card + node card render migration facts (Playwright against a REAL daemon); live drive: a real migration verified on a disposable PostgreSQL and applied to the PREVIEW environment - receipt + the `\dt` listing in a row comment.
Runbook + README; gates quoted with count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`.

implementationPlan.description: ADVERSARIAL PASS OVER THE COMPOSED FEATURE, recorded in a step note. (a) THE DATA-LOSS PATH, which is this row's reason for existing: confirm on the DELIVERED code that a failed `pg_dump` leaves ZERO migrations applied, and check the case no child owns — a backup that SUCCEEDS but writes a truncated or empty file. A zero-byte .sql with a recorded sha256 is a receipt that says 'backed up' and a file that restores nothing. (b) RESTORE ACTUALLY WORKS: child 3 was required to prove a restore round trip; read that evidence rather than the receipt's claim — a backup nobody restored is a file. (c) CONTAINER LEAKS UNDER CONCURRENCY: nodes now staff in parallel (task-92d84d38), so two verifications with disposable databases can run at once; confirm child 2's port strategy and teardown hold for two simultaneously, and that a crash between them leaves nothing behind. (d) THE SILENT-SKIP HOLE: confirm that on a machine WITHOUT docker a node cannot reach ACCEPTED through the database leg — that is the failure that would ship a schema change nobody ran, and it is invisible in a green suite. Where an answer is 'not covered', add it to the owning child's DoD or as a comment here (global rail 21).
implementationPlan.note:
ADVERSARIAL PASS over the composed feature, at HEAD d079210c. Detail and the three follow-ups are in comment-95965c48; verdicts here.

(a) THE DATA-LOSS PATH — CLOSED, and I did not take the receipt's word for it. In the DELIVERED code `ports.apply` is unreachable until `ports.dump` resolves AND the artifact hashes: migration-service.ts:63-65 runs dump -> hash -> apply in that order, and the catch at :67-73 (with backupRef still null) deletes the file and returns the base receipt, whose outcome is REFUSED with refusal MIGRATION_BACKUP_FAILED (:46). So a failed pg_dump = ZERO migrations applied. THE CASE NO CHILD OWNED — an empty backup with a recorded sha256 — is ALSO closed, by a guard I had to go find: backup-ports.ts:41-47 `backupFileHash` streams the file and throws on `size === 0`, and it is called at :64 BEFORE apply, so a zero-byte .sql refuses instead of producing a "backed up" receipt. RE-RUN LIVE, this session, on this host: `MOE_MIGRATION_RESTORE=1 pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run ... src/repository/migrations/migration-real.test.ts` EXIT 0, "Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 2 passed (2)", printing "REAL MIGRATION: schema changed, restored exactly, backup-failure unchanged, failing-file named" — that arm (migration-real.test.ts:87-98) injects a throwing `dump`, then asserts `schema()` is byte-identical to the pre-migration schema, the refusal is MIGRATION_BACKUP_FAILED@DAEMON_INGRESS, and `pgmigrations` still holds only the initial migration. Residual: a nonempty-but-TRUNCATED dump is not structurally validated (F1 in the comment) — guarded only by pg_dump's exit status and a failing close, not by reading the artifact.

(b) RESTORE ACTUALLY WORKS — PROVEN, by re-running the round trips rather than reading a claim. Same run as above: migration-real.test.ts:82-86 drops `public` CASCADE and feeds the RECORDED backup file (path taken from `backupRef` itself) back through psql, then asserts `schema()` equals the pre-migration schema exactly. Plus `MOE_MIGRATION_RESTORE=1 ... src/deployment/migrate-down-real.test.ts src/deployment/rollback-restore-real.test.ts` EXIT 0, "Test Files 2 passed (2) / Tests 4 passed (4)", printing "REAL MIGRATE_DOWN: last batch reverted, first batch standing, receipt recorded" (asserts the schema returns to the post-first-batch state, is NOT the post-second state, pgmigrations 2 -> 1, and the REVERTED receipt) and "REAL ROLLBACK RESTORE: recorded dump applied to the bound destination, mutation gone". These are real containers and a real PostgreSQL, not doubles.

(c) CONTAINER LEAKS UNDER CONCURRENCY — HOLDS for two simultaneous verifications; PARTIAL for a crash. Each DisposableDatabase takes a UUID name (verifier-database.ts:70), its own 32-byte password (:71) and an OS-assigned loopback port via `--publish 127.0.0.1:0:5432` + `docker port` (:117, :121-126), which is atomic and therefore TOCTOU-free under the parallel node staffing of task-92d84d38. Re-run live: `MOE_VERIFIER_DATABASE=1 ... src/orchestrator/verifier-database.test.ts` EXIT 0, "Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 21 passed (21)", printing "REAL VERIFIER CONCURRENT: two live databases, distinct ports/names, both removed" alongside ACCEPT / REJECT / FORCED RECIPE KILL / MIGRATION_FAILED, each ending "Docker says ABSENT" (asked of `docker ps --all`, never of an internal flag). `docker ps -aq` = 0 before and after all three of my runs. WHAT IS NOT COVERED: the container is `--detach` with NO `--rm`, so a SIGKILL of the daemon (or a host crash) between `docker run` and `cleanup()` leaves it alive, and nothing sweeps `moe-verifier-*` at boot (F2). One correction to the plan's risk framing: a leaked container does NOT wedge the next verification, because port 0 means the next run never asks for the leaked port.

(d) THE SILENT-SKIP HOLE — CLOSED, and the arm that proves it is composed, not unit-local. comments.content:
ADVERSARIAL PASS — THE THREE RESIDUAL GAPS, filed here as follow-ups (global rail 21) rather than as rows, because all three children are DONE and none of these makes delivered bytes non-working. Measured at HEAD d079210c by worker-812079a7, 2026-09-08.

F1 — A DUMP THAT IS NONEMPTY BUT INCOMPLETE IS NOT STRUCTURALLY CHECKED. The zero-byte case the architect named IS closed: apps/daemon/src/backups/backup-ports.ts:41-47 `backupFileHash` streams the artifact and `if (size === 0) throw fail()`, and migration-service.ts calls it at :64 BEFORE `ports.apply` at :65, so an empty dump refuses with backupRef still null and never applies a migration. What guards a HALF-WRITTEN dump is only (i) pg_dump's exit status — `docker()` at backup-ports.ts:53-58 throws on nonzero — and (ii) an error surfacing from `closeSync(output)` (dumpDatabase :85). Neither reads the artifact's CONTENT. A dump whose bytes were lost with a clean close and a zero exit would be hashed and recorded as a backup. CHEAP HARDENING, one arm and three lines: before hashing, assert the tail contains pg_dump's own terminator (`-- PostgreSQL database dump complete`, or the closing `\unrestrict` line the restore path already parses at :112-117). Not urgent: the realistic truncation causes (ENOSPC, container kill, network drop) all surface as a nonzero pg_dump exit or a failing close, and I re-ran the failed-dump arm live (below) to confirm zero migrations applied on that path.

F2 — NO ORPHAN-CONTAINER REAPER FOR `moe-verifier-*`. verifier-database.ts:116-118 starts the disposable database with `run --detach --name moe-verifier-<uuid> --publish 127.0.0.1:0:5432` and NO `--rm`; removal is in-process only (`dispose()`/`cleanup()` at :157-176, `finally` at :154, plus `close()` draining owners at :209-223). That covers every IN-PROCESS exit — ACCEPT, REJECT, forced recipe kill, cancel, and a failed `rm` is escalated to CONTAINER_CLEANUP_FAILED which sets `closed = true` so a known leak poisons new work (:198-201). It does NOT cover a SIGKILL of the daemon itself or a host crash between `docker run` and cleanup: that container keeps running and nothing ever sweeps it. `git grep "moe-verifier"` over apps/daemon/src finds the literal only at verifier-database.ts:70 (plus unrelated `moe-verifier-policy/1`), i.e. no boot-time or periodic sweep. Blast radius is bounded, and this is the one thing the architect's worry got backwards: because the port is bound with `:0` and reported back by `docker port`, a leaked container does NOT hold the port the next verification needs — the next run gets a fresh OS-assigned port. So the failure mode is accumulating stopped/running postgres containers and their volumes, not a wedged verifier. SUGGESTED: a boot sweep of `docker ps -aq --filter name=^/moe-verifier-` (or a `--label moe-verifier` + prune) in the wrapper's startup path. The deployment-side containers do NOT have this gap: `moe-backup-dump-*` / `moe-backup-apply-*` are `run --rm` (backup-ports.ts:78-84, :83) with `disposeContainer` in `finally`.

F3 — A STALE `.migration.lock` IS UNRECOVERABLE BY THE DOCUMENTED PROCEDURE. migration-service.ts:91-93 takes the lock with a bare `mkdirSync` and releases it in `finally` (:95-97); migration-down-service.ts:138-140 takes the SAME lock, deliberately, so an up and a down cannot interleave. The lock directory carries NO owner, pid or timestamp, and docs/agent-stack-runbook.md:286-287 tells the operator "Wait; do not delete the lock to force a second concurrent migration." If the daemon dies between `mkdirSync(lock)` and the `finally`, every later migrate and every later migrate_down refuses MIGRATION_IN_PROGRESS@DAEMON_INGRESS forever and the runbook's only instruction is to wait. SUGGESTED: stamp the lock with pid + ISO acquisition time and add ONE runbook paragraph naming the safe recovery (verify no migration process is live, then remove the lock). SECOND, smaller sharp edge in the same code: the lock lives at `dirname(<...>/backups/pre-migration/<env>)`, i.e. `.../pre-migration`, so it is PROJECT-WIDE across environments (the comment at :20-23 says so on purpose) — a PREVIEW migration therefore refuses a simultaneous PRODUCTION migration with MIGRATION_IN_PROGRESS. That is a defensible choice, but it is not stated in the runbook's operator-facing text and an operator will read the refusal as "someone is migrating THIS environment".

NOT GAPS, confirmed rather than assumed: (i) failed `pg_dump` leaves ZERO applied — `ports.apply` is unreachable until `dump` resolves AND the hash succeeds, and the catch at migration-service.ts:67-73 removes the file and returns the base REFUSED/MIGRATION_BACKUP_FAILED receipt; (ii) MIGRATION_FAILED still records the backupRef (:68) so the operator can restore, and the engine runs with `singleTransaction: true` (migration-ports.ts:40) plus a refusal of node-pg-migrate's own transaction escape (:34-37), so a throwing migration leaves nothing half-applied; (iii) two simultaneous verifications get distinct UUID names, distinct passwords and distinct OS-assigned ports; (iv) docker absent cannot reach ACCEPTED — see the step-4 note.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: REJECTED, planning this as one row: a scaffold change with a golden-tree bump, a verifier DATABASE leg with container lifecycle, a deploy-time backup-and-migrate path, a new human-only command with roster backfill, two UI surfaces, a Playwright journey and a live drive — far past the 12-step/10-file thresholds, so task rail 1 mandates the SPIDR split. REJECTED, making child 3 depend on the containerized-deployment row: it is a SIBLING feature row and the parent rail forbids that dependsOn — so child 3 composes with the deploy path if it exists and otherwise ships behind its own entry point, recording which. REJECTED, letting the database leg skip when docker is absent: a silent skip lets a node reach ACCEPTED with its migrations unrun, which is the worst outcome this feature can produce; it refuses with a code instead.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-20a6d1eb. THE GAP IS REAL: `grep -rn 'db:migrate|MIGRATION_' --include=*.ts apps/ packages/` finds only unrelated scheduler fairness constants (fairness-cap-revision.ts:53, fairness-aging.ts:110); the verifier runs the node's `test` recipe with NO database (node-verifier.ts, 230 lines; verifier-process-runner.ts, 395). WHAT TO REUSE RATHER THAN REINVENT: verifier-process-runner.ts already solves 'always clean up' for processes — injectable spawn/timeoutMs/killGraceMs/killProcessGroup (options :49-55), a process-GROUP SIGKILL (:187-189) and timer cleanup on every exit path (:110-114) — and child 2's container lifecycle should follow that shape. The BACKUP LOCATION already has a convention: activation-receipts-measure.ts:32-33 defines BACKUP_DIRECTORY '.moe-next' and BACKUP_LEAF 'backups', so `<project>/.moe-next/backups/<env>/<ts>.sql` extends an existing path rather than inventing a second place to look during an incident. TWO CROSS-ROW COORDINATIONS, neither expressible as dependsOn under the parent rail: the scaffold tree belongs to task-4a0f706437a042059789be2ebdb98bc0 (a profile VERSION BUMP, not an edit in place), and the deploy path plus the environment DATABASE_URL belong to task-5d309484... and task-9ae492b3...'s children. CONCURRENCY IS NOW NORMAL: parallel node staffing (task-92d84d38) makes two simultaneous verifications the ordinary case, so a disposable-database port strategy must survive it.
planningNotes.risks: BIGGEST RISK — losing data. Backup-before-migrate is the only thing between a bad migration and an unrecoverable production database, and the case no child's DoD names is a backup that SUCCEEDS but writes a truncated or empty file: a zero-byte .sql with a recorded sha256 produces a receipt saying 'backed up' and a file that restores nothing. Step 4(a) checks it. SECOND — a restore nobody has ever performed. Child 3 must prove a round trip; a backup that has only ever been written is a file, not a safety net. THIRD — the silent-skip hole: on a machine without docker, a database leg that skips instead of refusing lets a node reach ACCEPTED with its schema change unrun, and it is invisible in a green suite. That is why the refusal is a DoD clause and why step 3 asks whether the docker legs actually ran. FOURTH — leaked containers under concurrency: parallel staffing makes two disposable databases at once the normal case, and a leaked container holds its port so the NEXT verification fails far from the cause. FIFTH — conflating the two gate universes: the generated product's migration run and moe-next's own suite are different runs, and quoting one for the other would let a broken scaffold be reported green. SIXTH — timestamped migration filenames would break the scaffold's byte-identical golden test; child 1 must pin them.
